scope.standard_test_suite_omission_reason: This task permits only the report file to be written; existing tests create temporary package/cache/state files. No existing test pass count is claimed.

conclusion.verdict: P2 native inventory acceptance gap; P2 existing-suite discrimination gap with supplementary positive distinct-version rollback evidence; no demonstrated P1 host regression or broken rollback implementation
confirmed: installationIdentity omits unlisted skill and runtime paths. A supplied completed controlled-CLI reproduction returns success with skills/old-runtime/SKILL.md present.
Independent execution of the existing identity function against an in-memory filesystem confirms unchanged hashes for extra skill, extra root runtime, extra skill helper, and extra skill symlink.
The ordinary rollback fixture gives old cache, old recovery source and new candidate the same packed bytes, and mock plugin add normally never copies source bytes into the cache.

Parent reports a separate actual-copy controlled CLI probe passing distinct 0.8.1-to-0.8.2 upgrade and post-new-copy restoration of old 0.8.1 bytes. This is attributed supplemental evidence, not an independent rerun by this reviewer.
not_confirmed: An official CLI install/remove/update sequence actually retains extra files.
The official host discovers or loads the extra old-runtime skill.
An arbitrary extra runtime file starts a process or is otherwise reachable.
A real 0.8.1-to-0.8.2 or strict-to-native upgrade fails rollback or violates native behavior.
conclusion.why_not_p1: Known runtime paths are covered, the normal packer emits a clean four-file native package, and the extra filename in the reproduction is synthetic. Host retention, discovery and practical impact remain unverified. The evidence establishes a verification blind spot, not a high-impact production regression.
conclusion.goal_sensitive_classification: Under the native exact-one-skill/no-runtime goal, omitted skills deserve P2 because they may change the plugin interface. Under an explicitly limited critical-file comparison contract, unrelated inert files and unverified dependencies are design boundaries. Do not claim whole-tree integrity from the current digest.

findings.status: confirmed verifier gap; host impact conditional
findings.title: Fixed-path identity does not validate the native package inventory

evidence.note: Only fixed paths and top-level src/*.js enter the hash; regular-file and symlink checks run only on those paths. Native mode specifically rejects src and node_modules.
Candidate identity uses the same partial inventory.
Old cache and recovery source are compared using the same partial identity.
Installation succeeds after partial identity/version/digest checks; no exact skill or file inventory is checked.
Rollback also compares the same partial identity.
The manifest points skills at the entire ./skills/ directory; it does not name only skills/team.
The normal native packer emits exactly four files: manifest, package metadata, team skill and build info.
One-skill shape is asserted for a fresh packed output, not for the installed cache.
Native update coverage checks success and known src residue, but not arbitrary extra skill/runtime paths.
Smoke finds team positively and checks named residual paths; it does not assert the exact discovered skill set, and file count is only reported.

findings.behavior: Extra skills/old-runtime/SKILL.md, old-runtime.mjs, skills/team/scripts/helper.js or skills/old-runtime symlink do not affect installationIdentity. Known skills/strict-delivery/SKILL.md, .mcp.json, src and node_modules are covered; do not describe all runtime residue as invisible.
findings.impact: A cache can be accepted despite differing from the intended native package. Extra discoverable instructions could affect later collaboration; standalone unreferenced runtime files alone prove only extra payload, not execution.
findings.limits: No official-host inventory result was obtained. The broad skills manifest is a reason to test discovery, not proof of discovery.

findings.status: confirmed existing-fixture weakness; parent reports supplementary distinct-content upgrade and rollback success
findings.title: Rollback tests cannot distinguish restoration of old bytes from reuse of new bytes in their default fixture

evidence.note: One new package is built and copied into the old cache. previousVersion is usually only a 0.5.2 list-metadata label; actual package/build bytes remain current.
The old recovery source is copied from that same cache.
Mock remove changes state only; mock add invokes hooks and returns the same cache without installing selected marketplace contents.
Several restoration hooks copy from the NEW candidate, which happens to equal the old content.
A full-cache restoration hook likewise copies the NEW candidate.
The source/install/cache rollback loop therefore does not prove restoration after a distinct new package overwrote old bytes.
Same-version post-restore drift tests do provide meaningful negative identity checks.
Pre-mutation recovery-source and legacy checks remain meaningful.

findings.behavior: A simulated rollback that returns old metadata but leaves current candidate bytes can pass default tests because previousIdentity already describes those candidate bytes. In the corrupt-cache case, corruption happens before the old source is copied and before the old identity is taken; the mock install leaves those old bytes in place.
findings.surviving_value: The tests still exercise call ordering, metadata restoration, early preservation, known-file mismatch detection and explicit restoration-drift rejection. Calling the entire rollback suite invalid would be inaccurate.
findings.impact: The existing repository suite alone is insufficient evidence for real distinct-content rollback. The parent actual-copy probe now supplies positive controlled evidence for that path; no implementation failure is claimed.

design_boundaries.boundary: Dependencies and all unlisted runtime assets are not recursively fingerprinted.

evidence.note: The scope explicitly limits source/cache comparison to key files and excludes per-file dependency checking.
The recovery message explicitly limits its guarantee to key files and excludes full runtime dependency checking.

design_boundaries.classification: Declared design limitation for strict dependency integrity; do not escalate unrelated inert files to P1 without activation/reachability evidence. Native skill inventory is separately actionable because it is part of the advertised native interface.

design_boundaries.boundary: Concurrent external changes after a check are not excluded.

evidence.note: Post-check drift by other processes is already declared.

design_boundaries.classification: Known design limitation; this review does not propose an atomic transaction or broad updater rewrite.

minimal_protection.change: For build.mode === native, enumerate the small plugin tree with lstat, reject links and unexpected entry types, and enforce the exact allowed files plus their parent directories. Keep the existing critical-content hashing and rollback state machine.
minimal_protection.reason: One shared guard covers candidate validation, old cache/source preflight, installed cache and rollback verification. Comparing two full trees alone would still accept an equally polluted candidate/cache; the native shape invariant must also be enforced.
minimal_protection.compatibility: If the official host writes necessary sidecar files inside the plugin root, first establish those names from real receipts and permit only a narrow documented exception. No such sidecars were established in this review.
minimal_protection.cost: Native payload is four files, so bounded enumeration is a small local operation. No wall-clock or end-to-end speed claim is made.

minimal_protection.change: Construct valid old and new packages with intentionally different bytes, versions and digests; mock plugin add must copy the selected marketplace into its installed cache and derive metadata from that copy. Snapshot old bytes before mutation. Trigger failure only after asserting that new bytes have actually replaced old bytes.
minimal_protection.reason: Restoration of a distinct prior state must become necessary for the positive test to pass.

discriminating_regressions.setup: Clean native candidate; controlled install copies it, then adds one unexpected entry.
discriminating_regressions.expected: The installed cache is rejected and cleanup/rollback is verified. Each extra must be absent from the candidate so the test detects inventory mismatch.
discriminating_regressions.control: A clean four-file package still succeeds; known src and strict-delivery checks remain covered.

discriminating_regressions.setup: Independently pollute candidate, old cache, and old recovery source; also test identical unexpected entries in both sides of a comparison.
discriminating_regressions.expected: Native shape validation rejects before destructive plugin mutation. Equal pollution must not pass merely because two hashes match.
discriminating_regressions.control: Assert the call log contains no plugin removal/add for preflight failures and that old bytes remain unchanged.

discriminating_regressions.setup: Old native package A and new native package B have different valid version metadata, team skill text and source digest. Mock install really copies B. Inject a single failure after successful new-cache creation or during subsequent verification; recovery really copies A.
discriminating_regressions.expected: Assert new bytes existed before the failure, then compare restored cache bytes with the saved A snapshot and assert they differ from B. Check old marketplace, enabled state and version.
discriminating_regressions.negative_control: Make restoration falsely return old version metadata while copying/retaining B: updater must report recovery incomplete / old cache content not restored.
extensions: Repeat with equal version labels but different valid content/digests to prove content identity, not only version checks.
Include an omitted-installedPath list response with genuinely separate versioned cache paths.
Include strict-to-native A/B layouts if that upgrade path is part of the release acceptance target.

discriminating_regressions.setup: In a separately authorized temporary CODEX_HOME, reproduce the official CLI same-version and cross-version reinstall sequence with deliberate residue, then inspect the resulting cache inventory.
discriminating_regressions.expected: First establish whether the CLI preserves extras. Separately use host skills/list with forceReload to assert the exact plugin skill set; checking that team exists is insufficient.
discriminating_regressions.limits: Host enumeration requires a permitted host session. It was expressly prohibited in this review and was not run. Discovery still does not by itself prove an extra runtime process launches.

verification.mode: read-only static review plus in-memory execution of the unchanged installationIdentity function extracted from scripts/update.js
verification.tooling_note: The first harness attempt stopped at its extraction-boundary assertion before executing the function; trimming trailing whitespace corrected the harness, and the second run completed all nine cases. No product-source change was made.

high_reproduction.performance_limit: The reported approximately 3.16 ms is a controlled command-adapter result, not official CLI, host discovery, or model performance.

max.handoff: Bounded review complete. P2: native extra-skill inventory is omitted by fixed-path acceptance. Existing rollback fixture has P2 discrimination weakness, but parent actual-copy simulation passed distinct 0.8.1→0.8.2 update and restoration of old bytes after failure; this is not proof of a broken implementation. Minimum follow-up: exact native inventory guard plus preserve the distinct-content copying probe as a regression. Official CLI residue and actual host skill discovery remain unverified. No extra service or inference was started.
